renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: Cluster size distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts peptide clusters by the number of sequences they hold, split by the sample that contributed the representative. It answers how many AMP families are singletons and how many are large.
    How to read: many clusters of one member mean diverse, unrelated peptides. A long tail of large clusters means families found again and again, which are good candidates to look at first.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: members
    color: sample
    labels:
      members: Cluster size (sequences)
      sample: Sample
      count: Clusters

- component: card
  title: Largest cluster
  description: |-
    The hero number is the size of the largest cluster, and the bars rank the samples by the biggest cluster they contributed. It answers which families are the most widespread.
    How to read: a large cluster that spans several samples is a conserved peptide family. Check its representative in the table.
  column: members
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: largest cluster, by sample

- component: card
  title: Cluster size
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of sequences per cluster, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how redundant the peptides are.
    How to read: a median of one means most peptides are unique. A long upper whisker marks a few big families.
  column: members
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Peptide clusters table
  description: |-
    Each row is a cluster built by MMseqs2 with its representative sequence, the sample that contributed it and its number of members. It answers which families exist and how large they are.
    How to read: sort by members to find the biggest families.
    Source: https://ampcombi.readthedocs.io/en/main/about.html

- component: advanced_viz
  id: amp_embedding
  title: Property space of the AMP candidates
  description: |-
    Each point is an antimicrobial-peptide candidate placed by a principal component analysis of its physicochemical descriptors: molecular weight, isoelectric point, hydrophobicity and the helix, turn and sheet fractions, standardised first. The colour is the charge class. It answers which candidates resemble each other and how the charge classes separate.
    How to read: candidates close together share properties, and a group of one colour is a family with a common charge profile. Use the colour menu to colour by sample or by tool probability and see whether groups are sample specific.
    Lines and annotations: the charge class is a bin of the isoelectric point made by this catalog, basic at 8 or above and acidic at 6 or below, and not a call made by AMPcombi.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: cds_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: charge_class

- component: table
  title: Embedding coordinates table
  description: |-
    Each row is an AMP candidate with its two principal components, charge class, length and the probabilities of the prediction tools. It answers where a given candidate sits in property space.
    How to read: sort by a component to find the candidates at the edge of the cloud.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: amp_property_scatter
  title: Hydrophobicity against isoelectric point
  description: |-
    Each point is an antimicrobial-peptide candidate: its hydrophobicity on the horizontal axis and its isoelectric point on the vertical axis. The colour is the charge class and the size is the peptide length. It answers which candidates combine hydrophobicity with a positive charge.
    How to read: candidates in the upper right are hydrophobic and have a high isoelectric point, which means a positive net charge at neutral pH. Candidates in the lower part are acidic. Follow up the labelled points in the table.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. The charge class is a bin of the isoelectric point made by this catalog, basic at 8 or above and acidic at 6 or below, and not a call made by AMPcombi.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Hydrophobicity
    y_title: Isoelectric point (pI)
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: hydrophobicity
    y: isoelectric_point
    label: cds_id
    color: charge_class
    size: aa_length

- component: figure
  title: Candidates by best prediction probability
  description: |-
    Each point is a candidate placed by hydrophobicity and isoelectric point, coloured by the best probability any prediction tool gave it and sized by peptide length. It answers whether the candidates the tools trust most share a property profile.
    How to read: a cluster of bright points in one region means the tools agree on a property signature. Bright points far from the rest are confident candidates with unusual properties and worth checking in the table.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. AMPcombi sets a prediction score under its cut-off to zero, so the colour only grades candidates that passed at least one tool.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/nextflow_schema.json
  code: |-
    # keep the physicochemistry complete so no point is silently dropped
    df_modified = df.drop_nulls(["hydrophobicity", "isoelectric_point", "prob_max"])
  
    fig = px.scatter(
        df_modified.to_pandas(),
        x="hydrophobicity",
        y="isoelectric_point",
        color="prob_max",
        size="aa_length",
        size_max=18,
        opacity=0.75,
        color_continuous_scale="Tealgrn",
        hover_name="cds_id",
        custom_data=["sample"],
    )
    fig.update_layout(
        xaxis_title="Hydrophobicity",
        yaxis_title="Isoelectric point (pI)",
        coloraxis_colorbar_title="Best probability",
        margin={"t": 24, "l": 56, "r": 16, "b": 48},
    )

- component: card
  title: AMP candidates
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of candidates, and the ring splits them by charge class. The secondary number counts the samples that contributed one. It answers how many peptides the run predicts and what kind of charge they carry.
    How to read: the charge class is a bin of the isoelectric point made by this catalog, basic at 8 or above and acidic at 6 or below.
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: charge_class
  caption: candidates, by charge class
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: ampir probability
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median probability the ampir tool gave its candidates, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how confident that tool is about what it found.
    How to read: a median near one means a strong signal. AMPcombi sets a probability under its cut-off to zero, so a zero means the tool did not call that candidate.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: prob_ampir
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Peptide length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average length of the candidates in amino acids, and the histogram shows how lengths are spread. It answers what size of peptide the run predicts.
    How to read: a tail of long sequences deserves a second look. The pipeline has a minimum length parameter for AMPcombi, so the shortest candidates reflect the run's settings.
  column: aa_length
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: average, with its range

- component: card
  title: Best prediction probability
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average of the best probability any tool gave each candidate, shown against the prediction cut-off. It answers how confident the predictions are.
    How to read: an average above the cut-off means the typical candidate is a confident call. A low average with a high maximum means a few strong candidates among many weak ones.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is a probability of 0.6, the default of the nf-core/funcscan parameter that sets AMPcombi's amp cut-off. The run may set another value.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: prob_max
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.6
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: against the 0.6 probability cut-off

- component: table
  title: AMP candidates table
  description: |-
    Each row is an antimicrobial-peptide candidate with its tool probabilities, its physicochemical properties and its reference-database hit. It answers which candidates to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by best probability, then filter by charge class. A database hit with a high identity means the peptide is a known one.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: cds_id
